correctness.rationale: Every nonzero element of finite Rees M^0 lies in an ambient finite group if its diagonal sandwich entry is nonzero, otherwise its square is zero. A square-zero element in a commutative quotient annihilates every image: the reversed product vanishes when the forward product remains nonregular, and a regular image with absorbing-zero square is itself zero. For two regular images, if a cross sandwich entry vanishes their product dies; if both exist, triple sandwich products lie in both source maximal subgroups and force equal quotient identities. Thus distinct nonzero quotient groups are orthogonal and all remaining elements are annihilators. With no source zero the quotient is one abelian group. Direct diagonal injections plus two offdiagonal Brandt indices realize every listed structure. All group sizes and regular sandwich matrices are covered by this algebra; the 3616 finite quotient checker instances are corroboration, not completeness.

value.rationale: Equality of the commutative single-factor HS divisor classes is a natural nontrivial slice of the explicit Brandt and Rees divisor problems. It identifies a complete structural and constructive classification when arbitrary sandwich matrices could in principle enlarge divisor classes, and its key triple-product lemma is not a routine renaming of Brandt multiplication. The Brandt-only normal form/minimal-index theorem is correctly credited as prior.
